word-order.title: Korean word order (SOV)
word-order.summary: The verb always comes last. Everything else is flexible because particles carry the meaning.

sections.heading: Subject – Object – Verb
sections.explanation: English is Subject–Verb–Object: 'I eat bread.' Korean is Subject–Object–Verb: 'I bread eat.' Once you expect the verb at the end, most sentences stop feeling scrambled.

sections.heading: Particles do the work, so order can move
sections.explanation: Because 은/는 marks the topic and 을/를 marks the object, you can move those chunks around for emphasis and the sentence still means the same thing. Only the verb is locked to the end.

sections.heading: You can drop what's obvious
sections.explanation: Korean leaves out the subject whenever context makes it clear. A one-word answer is a complete sentence.

quiz.q: Where does the verb go in a Korean sentence?
Why can Korean move phrases around so freely?
opts: Because particles mark each word's role

topic-vs-subject.title: 은/는 vs 이/가
topic-vs-subject.summary: 은/는 sets the topic and invites contrast. 이/가 points at who exactly is doing something.

sections.heading: The shapes
sections.explanation: After a consonant use 은 and 이. After a vowel use 는 and 가. That is the only spelling rule you need.

sections.heading: 은/는: 'as for…'
sections.explanation: 은/는 announces what the sentence is about, and quietly compares it to something else. Use it to introduce yourself and to contrast two things.

sections.heading: 이/가: 'it is THIS one'
sections.explanation: 이/가 identifies the subject, especially new information or the answer to 'who?' and 'what?'. It is also required with 있어요/없어요 and with descriptive verbs like 좋다.

quiz.q: Which particle follows a word ending in a consonant, like 선생님?
You want to contrast: 'Coffee I like, but tea I don't.' Which particle marks 커피 and 차?

object-marker.title: The object marker 을/를
object-marker.summary: Mark the thing being acted on with 을 after a consonant, 를 after a vowel.

sections.heading: Which one to use
sections.explanation: 을 goes after a noun ending in a consonant; 를 after a noun ending in a vowel. The choice is purely about sound.

sections.heading: It attaches to the receiver of the action
sections.explanation: Whatever is being eaten, watched, bought or studied takes 을/를. Verbs of motion like 가다 use 에 instead, not 을/를.

sections.heading: In casual speech it disappears
sections.explanation: Spoken Korean drops 을/를 constantly when the meaning is obvious. Keep it in writing and in careful speech.

quiz.q: '책' ends in a consonant. Which object marker follows it?
Which sentence is correct for 'I drink coffee'?

to-be.title: 이에요 / 예요 — to be
to-be.summary: Attach 이에요 or 예요 to a noun to say 'is / am / are'.

sections.heading: Noun + 이에요/예요
sections.explanation: Use 이에요 after a consonant and 예요 after a vowel. There is no separate word for 'is' — it glues straight onto the noun.

sections.heading: Questions and negatives
sections.explanation: For a question, keep the same form and raise your intonation. For 'is not', use 이/가 아니에요.

sections.heading: Don't confuse it with 있어요
sections.explanation: 이에요/예요 means 'X is Y'. 있어요 means 'there is / I have'. They are not interchangeable.

quiz.q: '의사' ends in a vowel. Which form is correct?
How do you say 'I am not a student'?

present-tense.title: Present tense 아요 / 어요
present-tense.summary: Drop 다 from the dictionary form, then add 아요 or 어요 depending on the last vowel.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.explanation: Take the verb stem (dictionary form minus 다). If its last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, add 아요. Otherwise add 어요. 하다 verbs are irregular and become 해요.

sections.heading: When vowels merge
sections.explanation: If the stem already ends in ㅏ or ㅓ, the 아/어 is absorbed rather than doubled. 오 + 아요 contracts to 와요, and 우 + 어요 to 워요.

sections.heading: One form, three jobs
sections.explanation: 아요/어요 covers the present, the near future, and habitual actions. Intonation alone turns it into a question.

quiz.q: What is the present-tense form of 먹다?

opts: Stems whose last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ
Stems whose last vowel is ㅜ
